tool.name: file_upload_abuse_check
tool.description:
Probe a known multipart upload endpoint for the standard upload-bypass cohort. Iterates extension-switch / magic-byte-spoofing / content-type-spoofing / double-extension / null-byte / case-variant / SVG-XSS / HTML-XSS / path-traversal payloads and reports per-payload acceptance.
Invoked when the agent has already discovered an upload endpoint via crawl + form analysis. The caller provides the URL, the file form-field name, and any extra form fields (CSRF token, etc.) the endpoint requires.
Methodology (one HTTP request per probe, all bounded by `timeout`):
1. **Control upload** — `strix--control.jpg` (PNG magic bytes + minimal valid PNG body). Establishes baseline (status, body length, body hash). 2. **Bypass cohort** — 15 deterministic payload mutations (see table). Every payload carries `strix--` filename prefix so probe artifacts are auditable in target storage. 3. **Per-bypass verdict** — same status class as control AND body-length within ±25% = "accepted". For accepted bypasses, attempt fetch-back: extract any URL/path containing the nonce from the response, GET it, and check whether the body contains the probe marker AND the served Content-Type.
Bypass cohort:
| Class | Variants | |---|---| | extension switch | `.php`, `.phtml`, `.jsp`, `.aspx` | | magic-byte spoofing | PNG magic + PHP body, filename `.php` | | content mismatch | `.jpg` with PHP body | | double extension | `.php.jpg`, `.jpg.php` | | byte truncation | `.php\x00.jpg` | | case variant | `.PhP` | | filename normalization | `.php.`, `.php ` (trailing space) | | SVG / HTML XSS | `.svg` with ``, `.html` with `` | | filename injection | `../../../.txt` |
Severity tuning:
- **High** (CWE-434, unrestricted_upload) — server-executable extension accepted (`.php`/`.phtml`/`.jsp`/`.aspx`); OR fetch-back-confirmed dangerous Content-Type (`application/x-php`, `text/html` for SVG, etc.) without `Content-Disposition: attachment`; OR magic-byte-spoofed PHP accepted under `.php` filename. - **Medium** (CWE-434) — content-mismatch / double-extension / null-byte / case-variant / SVG/HTML XSS accepted without fetch-back confirmation. - **Low** (CWE-434) — path-traversal filename accepted (weak filename validation; not directly exploitable).
Per-class dedup: at most one finding per (severity × class) so a 4-variant extension-switch cohort generates one report, not four. Per-probe verdicts still live in the result dict for the agent.
Skip / soft-fail: - Control upload returns non-2xx/3xx → endpoint requires fields not supplied → tool exits with `inconclusive` and no probe traffic. - Cluster-A `--exclude-path` blocks the upload URL → graceful no-op.
Safety: - Every probe artifact has a unique `strix--` filename prefix (auditable + cleanable in target storage). - Payload bodies start with a clear test-artifact marker (`/* strix file-upload-abuse-check probe artifact - safe to delete */`). - Hard-capped at 4 KiB per probe — no DoS / decompression-bomb risk. - Read-only verification fetch-back (GET only, no follow-redirects, no execution). - Composes with cluster-A safety (auth-injection / exclude-path / rate-limit).
Each finding carries `description_plain` + `recommended_action` (validate file contents server-side via libmagic / file-type sniffing not filename or Content-Type; maintain extension allow-list; serve uploads from a separate sandboxed origin without script execution; force `Content-Disposition: attachment`; rename files server-side with a controlled extension). `verification_status=needs_review` since the heuristic relies on response-shape similarity to control + best-effort fetch-back; the agent should manually trigger any uploaded payload to confirm exploitability before treating any finding as confirmed RCE / XSS.

parameter.name: upload_url
parameter.description: The POST endpoint that accepts multipart/form-data uploads. Typically discovered via the BFS crawl + form analysis. Bare hostnames are auto-prefixed with `https://`. Examples: `https://app.example.com/api/upload`, `https://app.example.com/profile/avatar`, `https://app.example.com/documents/new`.

parameter.name: field_name
parameter.description: The form field name for the uploaded file. Default `file`. Common alternatives: `attachment`, `image`, `upload`, `avatar`, `document`, `photo`. The crawl + form analysis usually surfaces this from the `` HTML attribute.

parameter.name: extra_fields
parameter.description: Additional form fields the endpoint requires for a successful upload (CSRF token, document-type selector, target folder, etc.). Pass these verbatim — round-tripped on every probe. Example: `{"csrf_token": "abc123", "doc_type": "image"}`.

parameter.name: timeout
parameter.description: Per-probe timeout in seconds. Default 30 (accounts for slow upload-processing back-ends).

returns.description:
{success, upload_url, target_host, nonce, control: {status, status_class, body_length, accepted, error?, skipped?}, probes: [{label, class_, severity_if_accepted, filename, status, accepted, fetch_back: {url, status?, content_type?, disposition?, body_match?, skipped?}, finding_severity, evidence}, ...], findings_emitted}.
The agent should: 1. Confirm any `accepted=True` probe by fetching the artifact URL outside Strix (via Burp / browser) and checking server execution / rendering. 2. Clean up probe artifacts in target storage by searching for the `strix--` filename prefix returned in `nonce`.
